issues.title: Audio clip text overlaps waveform
issues.description: Attachment filename label renders directly on top of the audio waveform visualization.
issues.evidence: Filename text collides with waveform bars in the primary audio attachment.
issues.suggestion: Separate filename and waveform into dedicated flex containers with adequate vertical spacing.
issues.triageNote: Real: label/duration chips were absolutely positioned over the full-height waveform body. Fixed by moving chips into a dedicated header row above the media body.

issues.title: Double-rendered text in attachment card
issues.description: Text content in the third attachment card exhibits duplicated ghost rendering, making it illegible.
issues.evidence: Severely distorted duplicate text overlay visible across the document title label.
issues.suggestion: Clean up duplicate text nodes and pseudo-elements in the attachment component.
issues.triageNote: Real: text-kind clips rendered the caption row AND the absolute corner label chip on top of it. Fixed by inlining label/duration as chips in the single caption row (no overlay).

issues.title: Waveform and label overlap
issues.description: Clip title text and timestamp overlap directly with waveform graphics, impairing legibility.
issues.evidence: The 'room-tone.w..' text and '00:27' badge render on top of the audio waveform bars in the sequence track.
issues.suggestion: Separate clip metadata into a dedicated header row above the waveform canvas.
issues.triageNote: Real: same overlay root cause as pair-016; the header row now separates the room-tone label/00:27 chips from the waveform body.

issues.title: Premature label truncation
issues.description: Clip title truncates with ellipsis prematurely despite remaining inline container width.
issues.evidence: The second track clip shows 'intro-theme....' with empty space before the duration badge.
issues.suggestion: Adjust flex shrink and container max-width constraints on the label element.
issues.triageNote: Real: label chip had an arbitrary max-w-[70%] cap unrelated to the space actually left beside the duration chip. Fixed with a flex header row where the label truncates only once the row is genuinely full (at the 140px floor a long filename still truncates by design).
